title: Windows Security Event Log Cleared
detection_hypothesis: If an operator or adversary clears the Security log, the Security channel will contain the dedicated log-clear record even though the previous entries are gone.

field_semantics.EventID: Numeric identifier of the Windows event record.
field_semantics.Channel: Windows event log channel that carried the record.

collection_prerequisites: The relevant advanced audit policy subcategory is enabled for success events.
Domain controller Security logs are forwarded for directory-scoped events.
expected_collection_gaps: Events raised on a domain controller that is not forwarding logs are invisible.
Security log wrapping on busy controllers can drop events before forwarding.
normalization_assumptions: EventID is an integer and Channel is the literal string Security.
Account names are provided without the domain prefix in TargetUserName.
ingestion_differences: Some pipelines rename EventID to event.code or similar.
Directory attribute events may arrive with XML-encoded values.
retention_considerations: Security log volume varies widely; 180 to 365 days is common for identity events.
expected_volume: Rare; every production match deserves triage.
false_positive_strategy: Benign clears happen on build and imaging hosts, performed by imaging service accounts, and correlate with a machine rebuild. Tune with the host role and the subject account rather than suppressing the event.
tuning_guidance: Restrict any exclusion to the imaging build hosts and the imaging service account. Never exclude this event across the production estate.
test_strategy: Positive cases clear the log from two different accounts. Negative cases use a different event identifier, a different channel, and an ordinary logon record.

attack_techniques.name: Impair Defenses: Clear Windows Event Logs

author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
